rows.text: Well, one of the things that caves does is it's an analog to flying to space and In particular to flying to remote places like the moon.
rows.title: Fifty Years of Mars Imaging: from Mariner 4 to HiRISE
rows.license: public domain (NASA media; no endorsement implied)

rows.text: So what we did I arrived there around September 11th And we did about five or six days of training on how to repel and ascend in and out of a cave shaft We also visited several caves in Slovenia.
rows.title: EXPEDITION 68 SPACE STATION CREW PREPARES FOR LAUNCH IN KAZAKHSTAN
rows.license: public domain (NASA media; no endorsement implied)

rows.text: So the analog to space is that if and when we go back to the moon we would do similar things on the moon where we'd have to work together in a high-threat environment as a group, as a team to explore
rows.title: International Observe the Moon Night - Sept. 26 2020
rows.license: public domain (NASA media; no endorsement implied)
rows.preview: https://images-assets.nasa.gov/video/NHQ_2020_0914_Observe the moon promo/NHQ_2020_0914_Observe the moon promo~medium.jpg

rows.text: And so going back to the moon 2024, it's very soon, very quick, and I think everyone in the astronaut corps is prepared for that.
rows.title: NASA astronaut Woody Hoburg prepares a spacesuit for a spacewalk
rows.license: public domain (NASA media; no endorsement implied)

rows.text: And Caves is one of those tools that will help you prepare to go to the moon, do research exploration, stay on the moon, and have a permanent presence there.
rows.title: Seven Possible Cave Skylights on Mars
rows.license: public domain (NASA media; no endorsement implied)

rows.text: And so in the meantime what NASA has going is we have two commercial crew vehicles that are being developed to take astronauts to the International Space Station.

rows.text: The Earth's atmosphere is divided into layers the lowest at the lowest layer is what we call the troposphere and

rows.text: temperatures decrease as you go upward into the troposphere You eventually reach a point where it's incredibly cold In fact interestingly enough some of the warmest temperatures that we see at the gro

rows.text: also some of the coldest temperatures that we see in the world are found about 50 ,000 feet above the ground in the tropics.

rows.text: So here it's getting down to temperatures of about minus 110 degrees below zero.

rows.text: So there's a huge decrease in temperature and this is all occurring in the troposphere.

rows.text: And the troposphere is where we find most of our weather, all the cloud systems, are down here in the troposphere.

rows.text: Now you get to the stratosphere, that's this layer, and temperatures begin to increase.

rows.text: The tropopause separates the troposphere from the stratosphere.

rows.text: Most of the ozone in our atmosphere is found up here in the stratosphere.

rows.text: We call this the ozone layer.

rows.text: Now this is an invisible form of light it can't be seen and this is a very damaging form of light it can cause skin cancer for example but it's mainly absorbed here by the ozone layer.
